subject: Mutual action plan + load test schedule for OliveTech evaluation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Mutual action plan + proposed load test window for OliveTech evaluation

Hi Alice / Markus —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation I attached a short Mutual Action Plan (OliveTech_MAP_v1.pdf) and a proposed evaluation & load-testing plan so we can validate latency and throughput targets for the embeddings + reranker endpoints before you commit to Dedicated capacity. High level asks: please review the MAP and confirm the proposed test window (week of Feb 21).

Quick summary of the evaluation plan included in the attachment:
- Scope: embeddings endpoint (embedding vector generation) and reranker endpoint (embedding+cross-attention reranker).
- Workloads: 5k unique queries replayed across three run types: baseline (steady load), stress (peak-surge), and soak (long duration).
- Metrics we will measure: p50/p95 latencies, TTFT (time-to-first-token for reranker), sustained throughput (qps), end-to-end concurrency and system CPU/GPU utilization.
- Payload sizes: queries sampled at avg. 64 tokens, long-tail up to 512 tokens; reranker evals include 128 candidates per query.
- Warm-up: 15 minute warm-up with cache priming and small-scale replay.
- Test infra: load generators from GCP us-west1, results captured to perf_results_run3.csv and Grafana dashboards.

Please confirm:
1) Approved MAP and test window (we proposed Feb 21–24).
2) A contact on your infra/security side to whitelist our load generator IPs and provide any network constraints.
3) Any change to expected query payload distribution (we used the sample set you shared).

Next steps once approved: we’ll schedule a brief kickoff (30m) to walk through the runbook, share the k6 load spec and provide the sample payloads.

Thanks —
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan + proposed load test window for OliveTech evaluation

Alice — thanks, Feb 22–23 works for us. Confirming items and adding the run-level schedule below. We will provide load generators from GCP us-west1 to keep measurements consistent, but if you prefer to run from your account we can provide the k6 spec and environment templates.

Run plan (Tue Feb 22 — Embeddings; Wed Feb 23 — Reranker):
- 09:00–09:30: Kickoff & network check, whitelisted IP verification (we’ll provide a short script to validate connectivity).
- 09:30–09:45: Warm-up: 15 mins, progressive ramp to 10% of target qps. Cache priming (prefix KV cache enabled).
- 09:45–11:00: Baseline run: steady-state at target qps for 75 minutes (measure p50/p95, GPU utilization).
- 11:15–11:45: Stress run: short spike to 2–3x target qps for 30 minutes (observe queuing, TTFT).
- 12:00–14:00: Soak run: 2 hours at 80% of target to observe memory growth/leaks.

Measurement notes:
- We will capture server-side TTFT (per-request server log) and client-observed end-to-end latencies.
- For reranker we will report both single-query rerank latency and batch-rerank throughput (where we score 32 queries per batch).
- All raw traces will be uploaded to the shared drive; summarized CSV in perf_results_run3.csv.

Marissa / Karthik — tagging you for any model/config guidance before we lock the run.

Ben
(Attachment: load_config.yaml)

Couple of recommendations before the run — please add these as constraints in the MAP and call them out in the kickoff: 

Model/config:
- Embeddings: use model: redwood-embed-2.1 (int8 quantized), sequence length capped at 512 for batch ops. Expected baseline: p95 < 150ms at ~1k qps when KV cache warm.
- Reranker: use model: redwood-rerank-1.4 (fp16), deployed on A100 80GB instances with 8k context. Expect p95 < 350ms at 150–200 qps for the 128-candidate rerank workload.

Operational:
- Enable prefix caching on the reranker and allow 15–20 minute warm-up prior to reporting baseline numbers.
- Capture per-token kernel time and GPU occupancy (we need traces to diagnose tail behavior).
- Please run one cold-start trial (no cache) to capture TTFT baseline.

Acceptance thresholds (for this evaluation to move to Dedicated talk):
- Embeddings: median < 40ms, p95 < 150ms at steady-state expected load.
- Reranker: TTFT median < 60ms, p95 < 350ms at expected throughput.

I added these notes to the MAP doc in the sharepoint link.

-Marissa

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan + proposed load test window for OliveTech evaluation — results attached

Alice / Markus —

Thanks again for running the sessions with us. Attached is a concise benchmark summary and the raw CSV (perf_results_run3.csv). High-level results below, followed by recommended next steps. Numbers reflect the reported client-observed latencies and server TTFT captured during the baseline runs (after the recommended warm-up).

Embeddings endpoint (redwood-embed-2.1, int8) — steady-state @ 1,000 qps:
- Median latency (client): 24 ms
- p95 latency (client): 128 ms
- Sustained throughput: 1,000 qps (stable during 75-minute baseline)
- GPU utilization (A100 pool): 62% average

Reranker endpoint (redwood-rerank-1.4, fp16, 128 candidates) — steady-state @ 180 qps:
- TTFT median (server): 48 ms
- p95 end-to-end latency (client): 312 ms
- Sustained throughput: 180 qps with batch size 4 across worker nodes
- Observed tail spikes when concurrency > 256: queue latency increased by ~40–60%

Stress findings:
- At 2.5x target qps embeddings remained functional but p95 increased to ~420 ms and we saw queue drops after 90s of sustained spike.
- Reranker at 3x load degraded quickly; recommend autoscaling thresholds and backpressure on client.

Recommendations to proceed toward Dedicated capacity:
1) Start with 2 dedicated A100 nodes for reranker pool to keep buffers small and tail low; scale the embeddings pool horizontally.
2) Enable longer KV cache lifetimes for reranker candidate prefixes to reduce TTFT for repeated patterns.
3) Instrument per-kernel traces for any further tail analysis — we’ve uploaded a sample trace to the sharepoint link.

Next steps we propose:
- I’ll update the MAP with the measured numbers and proposed Dedicated sizing.
- If OliveTech is comfortable we can move the deal to the engineering intake for Dedicated sizing and SOW prep.

Files attached: perf_results_run3.csv (raw), OliveTech_MAP_v1.pdf (updated with results). HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Ben Carter
